title: Press launch for Give Peace A Chance by Plastic Ono Band | 1969
content:
A press launch event for the first Plastic Ono single, ‘Give Peace A Chance’, was held on 3 July 1969.

John Lennon and Yoko Ono did not attend, as they were in hospital in Scotland following their car accident on 1 July.

The press launch took place at Chelsea Town Hall in London, with 300 attendees. In the Lennons’ absence, Ringo Starr and Maureen Starkey stepped into the breach.

We held a press reception in Chelsea Town Hall for the new single, the first by a group now known as The Plastic Ono Band. We displayed Charlie Melling’s model of the band, commissioned by John and Yoko and me from Charlie’s Hoylake workshop. Smaller world than ever…?

John and Yoko were not present at the reception. During a holiday tour of Scotland – just the two of them, with the little ones, Kyoko Ono Cox and Julian Lennon – their car had been involved in a nasty collision. All those flights and dangers abroad safely over, they had Brushed With Death at home. The reception crowd was disappointed but not badly so, being quite drunk, later doing the conga to round off the evening. I made a speech from the stage of the town hall announcing the accident. What I didn’t announce was the death a few hours earlier of our friend Brian Jones, late of The Rolling Stones: drowned in the swimming-pool of his home, AA Milne’s House at Pooh Corner. I did, however, murmur some reflective aside about the nearness of tragedy and from the audience someone shouted, ‘Bollocks!’ It was one of my ex-secretaries, full of challenge and Apple hospitality. We later apologized to each other; she for the shouting, I for the maundering. End of party.

Derek Taylor
Fifty Years Adrift
